title: Traffic in Erlangs and the chance of a busy signal
instructions:
## Sizing the trunks

A small exchange sees **120 calls per hour**, each lasting **3 minutes** on average, over **10 trunks**. The Erlang B formula gives the blocking probability B(E, N) = (Eᴺ/N!) ÷ Σₖ₌₀ᴺ (Eᵏ/k!).

1. The offered traffic in Erlangs.
2. The blocking probability with 10 trunks, as a percentage (two decimals).
3. The carried traffic (offered × (1 − B)).
4. The average trunk utilisation as a percentage.
hints: Erlangs = calls per hour × average holding time in hours = 120 × 3/60.
Compute the terms 6ᵏ/k! for k = 0…10 and sum them; the last term over the sum is B.
realityNote: Operators design for a grade of service of 1–2% blocking at the busy hour; here 10 trunks give 4.3%, so an 11th trunk would be added. The same formula sizes call-centre agents and cell-site channels.
